claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was the bishop of the Syrian city of Gabala and lived approximately from 355 to 408/425.
He became a well‑known preacher in Constantinople around the year 400 and continued to be active there until about 404.
Severian was a chief opponent of John Chrysostom and took part in the Synod of the Oak that led to Chrysostom’s deposition.
The sermon reflects the Antiochene school’s literal approach to Scripture, emphasizing concrete moral and theological teaching rather than allegorical interpretation.

The text survives in the Greek Patrologia Graeca (volume 56) and in a seventh homily preserved only in the 1613 Eton edition of John Chrysostom’s works, where it was mistakenly attributed to Chrysostom.
Modern critical editions have been produced, such as the editio princeps and Russian translation of the homily on Genesis 1:26 (CPG 4234), confirming the manuscript tradition.
